clue.text: Out of bed to court contemporary

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone getting up early to go and woo a person of their own generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contemporary is current and modern, exactly what the idiom for being abreast of the times conveys.

clue.text: Wild encore drowns second encore

indicators.note: to drown something is to submerge it, so one piece goes down inside the other
wild suggests the letters of the word encore running out of control into a new order

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an informal second

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic audience's shout for more swamps the request for a second encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' and 'drowns' are both indicators; MO is informal for a moment. The setter uses 'encore' twice, once as letters and once as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting the French word at a performer is a call for them to repeat the piece again.

clue.text: He boasted about being caught in fog and arrived too late

indicators.note: something caught in a thing is held inside it, so these letters sit within the other piece

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the words he boasted turning around into a new order

explanation.surface: A braggart got lost in the fog and turned up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means concerning; it is the anagram signal, and 'being caught in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes failing to catch a chance or a departure through arriving after it has gone.

clue.text: Base soldier comes up with prize for tail twisting

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the tail end of the prize's name is twisted, its last two letters changing places

parts.note: the Nobel is a famous prize

explanation.surface: A lowly soldier wins an award for twisting someone's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses GI to IG; 'tail twisting' swaps the last two letters of NOBEL to make NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the moral sense means dishonourable or mean, a synonym for lacking nobility of character.

clue.text: Wild hen parties are missing courage to play this?

indicators.note: wild suggests the remaining letters of hen parties running riot into a new order
missing tells us the letters of the word are are lacking from the fodder

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Rowdy hen parties need some nerve to play a kissing game.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A, R, E out of HEN PARTIES and 'Wild' rearranges the remaining HNPTIES into SPINTHE. A hen party is a British bride-to-be's night out with her friends.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a party game in which a spun bottle picks who must kiss or take a dare.

clue.text: With 22, like this one visible rag?

indicators.note: with read as having: the word for visible has the cleaning cloth held within it; the setter gives no stronger signal

parts.note: something visible is in sight
a rag used for cleaning is a wiper

explanation.surface: On the dating app, approving of the profile of someone reading a showy newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With 22' points to TINDER, the dating app, where this gesture marks a profile as liked; the container is only implied by 'With' (having), as the clue has no clearer signal.
explanation.definitionFit: On dating apps the rightward gesture across the screen registers approval of the profile shown.

clue.text: A left ear — and ear's sexy!

indicators.note: left as in departed, so the letter A has gone away from the word ear

parts.note: otic means of or relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A silly ode to ears, declaring them alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A left' removes A from EAR, leaving ER; OTIC is the adjective for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy and erotic are synonyms for arousing desire.

clue.text: Ability to buy, until replacing shop contents wore off

indicators.note: replacing tells us one piece goes in where something else is taken out
the contents of the word shop are its inner letters, which are the part swapped out

parts.note: pending can mean until, as in pending a decision

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of wore going awry into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper's money lasts only until the novelty of the shop's stock fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing shop contents' swaps the inner HO of SHOP for PENDING, giving S-PENDING-P; 'off' rearranges WORE into OWER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the economists' term for the money and credit a person or group has available to purchase goods.

clue.text: See 8

Why potions get mixed, as instructed in the Old Testament

definitions.text: as instructed in the Old Testament

indicators.note: potions are naturally mixed, so the letters of why potions are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking why potions are mixed in line with biblical instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Deuteronomy repeatedly orders 'thine eye shall not pity', so this is a fair description of an Old Testament command.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuteronomy commands the Israelites to be merciless, phrasing it as an instruction against compassion.

clue.text: Sharp boozer needs a place to sleep

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, or bar
a bed is a place to sleep

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued drinker needs somewhere to crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in the sense of a cutting remark, or literally a hook or wire with spikes.

clue.text: Bill's partner imprisoned by outlaws (Australians)

indicators.note: one piece is locked up inside the other

parts.note: bandits are outlaws
lovers bill and coo, so coo is the partner of bill

explanation.surface: A man named Bill's partner jailed by Australian outlaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is the bird's beak sense in the phrase 'bill and coo'.
explanation.definitionFit: These small marsupials are native to Australia, so they are Australians in the animal sense.

clue.text: With reduced fat and sugar + 7 = two Rs

parts.note: lite is the labelling term for food with reduced fat and sugar
the answer to 7 down means sexy, as does racy

explanation.surface: Reads like a diet recipe sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs of basic education are reading, writing and arithmetic; reading and writing together make up two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading and writing ability is two of the three Rs of schooling, the third being arithmetic.

clue.text: See 5
Set up an unusual source of protein

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of set up an being put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone launching an odd new protein supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' looks like a reversal instruction; the words are simply part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundnuts are legumes rich in protein, a common source for vegetarians.

clue.text: See 3
Serious four score at shallow end

indicators.note: the end of the word shallow is its final letter

parts.note: a score is twenty, so four score is eighty

explanation.surface: A serious swimmer scoring four points at the shallow end of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious matter is a heavy, important one, the figurative sense of having great weight.

clue.text: Time to drink and eat?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer's second word breaks up the first, giving these clue letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is a pause for refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: TEA broken up makes EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A work pause for a cuppa is a short interval when people stop for a hot drink.

clue.text: Heave supporting stone for a period

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight
to heave is to retch

explanation.surface: Struggling to lift a stone for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heave' looks like lifting the stone; it is the gagging sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is a continuous span of time, as in a long stretch of service.

clue.text: Posted filth back inside — that's harsh

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: posted means sent, as with a letter

indicators.note: back means the letters of the word for filth are read in reverse

parts.note: dirt is filth

explanation.surface: Someone sending dirt back in the post, a harsh act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal and 'inside' the container; 'Posted' is the past tense, matching the past-tense SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or tone is loud and grating, a synonym for harsh.

clue.text: Kindling for romance?

definitions.meaning: dry material used to light a fire
the dating app people use when looking for love

explanation.surface: Something that lights a fire, or sparks love.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry kindling catches fire easily, and the dating app of the same name is where many romances are sparked.

clue.text: Take a punt with light shop

parts.note: to take a punt is British slang for to bet
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Gambling on a lamp shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is the British slang verb meaning to inform on someone to the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is to inform on them, which betrays their trust.

clue.text: See 5
Mostly understanding about old man's body, mortician leads funeral

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an entente is an understanding between nations

indicators.note: the leading letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A mortician leading a funeral procession, with a grasp of the old man's remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the treaty word; 'leads' takes first letters of four words; 'about' wraps the shortened word round them. An entente is an understanding between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a body in a tomb is the burial at the heart of a funeral.

clue.text: See 3
See 26 down
It means happiness for sad creature

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a bird is a creature

explanation.surface: A paradox: a happy symbol for a melancholy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The bluebird of happiness is a traditional emblem of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore and song make this small songbird a symbol of contentment and joy.

clue.text: Right to take a break with cart in river, overturned in a kind of fluid

indicators.note: overturned means the whole construction is read backwards

parts.note: a lull is a break in activity

indicators.note: the cart goes into the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Someone taking a rest while their cart tips over into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container and 'overturned' reverses the whole build at the end. The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid outside the body's cells is classed this way, so the term names a kind of bodily fluid.
